# Engram

> Engram is an open-source (MIT) context graph for coding agents, built on FalkorDB. It turns a repository into one graph of code (files, symbols, calls, imports), git history (commits, authors, co-change) and agent memory (sessions, reads, edits, lessons, verify commands, edit claims), and gives the agent a ~200-token map of likely `file:lines` locations before its first tool call. It makes no LLM calls of its own; every answer is a Cypher query.

Measured results (Claude Code headless, claude-haiku-5-5, same model and bugs with and without Engram):
- pallets/click, 12 injected bugs x 3 repeats (144 runs across 4 setups): -25% mean input tokens, -29% tool calls, -23% time; 35/36 fixed vs 36/36 baseline.
- networkx (128k lines), 6 bugs x 1 repeat: -24% input tokens, -40% tool calls, -36% time.
- yt-dlp, 30 real GitHub issues, zero LLM tokens: right file in the top 3 for 22/30. Live Claude Code on 4 of them: -31% tokens, -33% tool calls.
Raw data for every number is in the repository under bench/results.

Install (macOS on Apple silicon, Linux x64/arm64 with glibc 2.39+): `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManojRakshu/engram/main/install.sh | sh` inside a repo. Windows x64, natively in PowerShell: `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManojRakshu/engram/main/install.ps1 | iex`. No Docker, database server or API keys; FalkorDB runs embedded (FalkorDBLite). Connects Claude Code (plugin with hooks), Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, opencode, VS Code, Cline, Kiro and any MCP client.

- [Cypher queries](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManojRakshu/engram/main/docs/CYPHER.md): every query and graph algorithm the product depends on
- [Comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManojRakshu/engram/main/docs/COMPARISON.md): results, setup, speed and resources vs codebase-memory-mcp, and where Engram is behind
